messages.subject: model selection - marginal WAIC
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I am trying to undertsand better how to do model selection in Nimble when random effects are included. To my understanding, marginal WAIC should be used over conditionnal WAIC when models have latent variables. 
My questions are:
1- In the modified example below from the AHM book, did I get the grouping right to calculate marginal WAIC? (controlWAIC parameters are correct?) 
2- When comparing models with vs. without random effects, how to calculate marginal WAIC for models without latent variables? what the parameters of controlWAIC would look like in the example below if alpha0 is fixed ? 

Thanks a lot,

require(AHMbook)
require(nimble)
data("crestedTit")

# Prepare data object
C <- as.matrix(crestedTit[, 6:23]) # matrix of counts
M  <-  nrow(C)
elev <- as.numeric(scale(crestedTit$elev)) # site elevation
forest <- as.numeric(scale(crestedTit$forest)) # site forest cover

# Bundle data
win.data <- list(C = C, M = nrow(C), J = ncol(C), elev = elev, forest = forest, elev.forest = elev * forest)

# Specify model in BUGS language
# Code modified from file "RE.Poisson.txt" from AHM code

section5p13_code <- nimbleCode( {
# Priors
mu.alpha ~ dnorm(0, 0.001) # Mean hyperparam
tau.alpha <- pow(sd.alpha, -2)
sd.alpha ~ dunif(0, 10) # sd hyperparam

for(k in 1:3){
alpha[k] ~ dunif(-10, 10) # Regression params
}

# Likelihood
for (i in 1:M){
alpha0[i] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha, tau.alpha) # Random effects and hyperparams

for(j in 1:J){
C[i,j] ~ dpois(lambda[i,j])
log(lambda[i,j]) <- alpha0[i] + alpha[1] * elev[i] + alpha[2] * forest[i] + alpha[3] * elev.forest[i]
}
}
})

# Other model run preparations
inits <- list(alpha0 = rnorm(M), alpha = rnorm(3)) # Inits
params <- c("mu.alpha", "sd.alpha", "alpha0", "alpha") # Params
ni <- 3000 ; nt <- 25 ; nb <- 1000 ; nc <- 2 # MCMC settings

# build model
Rmodel0 <- nimbleModel(code=section5p13_code, constants=win.data, inits=inits)
Cmodel0 <- compileNimble(Rmodel0)

# MCMC configuration and building
Groups <- c(paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",1]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",2]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",3]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",4]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",5]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",6]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",7]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",8]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",9]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",10]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",11]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",12]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",13]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",14]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",15]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",16]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",17]"),
paste0('lambda[', 1:267,",18]"))

mcmcspec0 <- configureMCMC(Rmodel0, monitors=c("mu.alpha", "sd.alpha", "alpha0", "alpha"), enableWAIC=TRUE,
controlWAIC =list(dataGroups = Groups, marginalizeNodes = 'alpha0'))
pumpMCMC0 <- buildMCMC(mcmcspec0,thin=nt)

# Compile MCMC
CpumpMCMC0 <- compileNimble(pumpMCMC0, project= Rmodel0)

# run model
mcmc.CM0 <- runMCMC(mcmc=CpumpMCMC0,
niter = ni,
nburnin = nb,
nchains = nc,
WAIC=TRUE)

# Check some results
require(MCMCvis)
MCMCsummary(mcmc.CM0$samples, params='alpha0', round = 2)

### Check marginal WAIC
mcmc.CM0$WAIC
